Drought and water scarcity

14 March 2025
Share on social media Print this page

Key facts

  • An estimated 2.3 billion people live in countries that are under high water stress.
  • Drought affected at least 55 million people directly in 2024, more than any other natural hazard.
  • By 2030, up to 700 million people could be displaced by intense water scarcity.

Overview

Drought is a prolonged dry period in the natural climate cycle that can occur anywhere in the world. It is a slow-onset disaster characterized by the lack of precipitation, resulting in a water shortage for people, crops and livestock.

Drought is a prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall that leads to a shortage of water, and it affected 55 million people in 2024. Its impacts compound over time: crop failure, loss of livestock and the spread of water-borne disease.

Who is affected

Water stress is unevenly distributed. The table below shows the number of people living in areas classified as high or extremely high water stress, by region, for the year 2024.

RegionPeople in high water stressShare of population
Sub-Saharan Africa430 million36%
South Asia1.1 billion57%
Middle East and North Africa390 million83%

Women and girls bear a disproportionate burden: in households without piped water, they are responsible for collecting water in 8 out of 10 cases.

Response

Countries are shifting from crisis management toward proactive drought risk reduction, including early warning systems, groundwater monitoring and drought-resilient agriculture. Since 2019, 71 countries have adopted national drought plans.
